test_cases.Feature: AHB interface to access its register space
test_cases.Test Description: Verify that all controller registers have expected reset values and that writable fields accept writes while non-writable fields retain their reset values according to the defined masks.
test_cases.Remarks: Unreadable register locations are skipped based on the read mask. Unwritable locations are skipped based on the write mask. Entries explicitly listed in the skip array are not accessed.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: Start the test case.

Perform default value verification over the configured register list: for each register entry in the list, if the location is marked readable, read its value; compare the read value with the documented default for that entry; record a default mismatch failure if any comparison does not match.

Perform write/read verification using six data patterns across the configured register list: for each test pattern, for each register entry, if the entry is not in the skip list and marked as writable, write the pattern to that register.

After writing a pattern, for each register entry that is not skipped and marked as both writable and readable, read back the value; compute the expected value by combining the written pattern over writable and readable bits with the preserved reset value over bits that are not writable but readable; compare the read value to this expected value; record a write/read mismatch failure if any comparison does not match.
Determine overall result: if no default mismatches and no write/read mismatches are recorded, report pass; otherwise, report fail.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: During default value checks: a pass requires that each readable entry returns its documented default value.

During write/read checks: for each writable and readable entry, a pass requires the read value to equal the expected value computed from the written pattern over writable readable bits combined with preserved default values over non-writable readable bits.
Overall pass requires zero default mismatches and zero write/read mismatches; any nonzero failure count results in fail.
test_cases.Hidden_Test_Description: Test verifies default register values via chk_rst_val() and performs masked write/read verification via chk_rd_wr() across CNT=43 I2C register addresses defined in addr_array[]. Six patterns are written where permitted and read back to validate masked behavior; failures increment def_fail_cnt and wr_fail_cnt; finish(0) on success else finish(1).
test_cases.Hidden_Remarks: Addresses with read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000 are skipped for reading. Addresses with write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000 are skipped for writing. Addresses with skip_array[i] == 1 are skipped for both writing and reading as encountered.
Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure: test_case(): call chk_rst_val(); call chk_rd_wr(); if (def_fail_cnt > 0 || wr_fail_cnt > 0) finish(1) else finish(0).

chk_rst_val(): for (i=0; i<CNT; i++): addr = addr_array[i]; if (read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue; data_rd = read_reg(addr); if (data_rd == default_value_array[i]) pass else def_fail_cnt++ and print failure.

chk_rd_wr(): define chk_val[6]={0xffffffff,0xaaaaaaaa,0x55555555,0x00000000,0xA5A5A5A5,0xffff0000}; For each j in 0..5: data_wr = chk_val[j]; Write phase: for (i=0; i<CNT; i++): addr = addr_array[i]; if (skip_array[i] == 1) continue; if (write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue; else write_reg(addr, data_wr).

Read/compare phase: for (i=0; i<CNT; i++): addr = addr_array[i]; if (skip_array[i] == 1) continue; if (write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue; if (read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue; else data_rd = read_reg(addr); wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff); exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])); if (data_rd == exp_val) pass else wr_fail_cnt++ and print failure.
test_cases.Hidden_Validation_Acceptance_Criteria: Pass if for all i where readable, read_reg(addr_array[i]) == default_value_array[i] in chk_rst_val(); and for each pattern in chk_rd_wr() and each i where both readable and writable (and not skipped), read_reg(addr_array[i]) equals exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | ((write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff) & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])). Any increment of def_fail_cnt or wr_fail_cnt causes finish(1).

test_cases.Test Description: Validate end-to-end transfer from controller instance 0 (master) to controller instance 1 (slave) using DMA for transmit and receive with interrupt-driven completion, followed by data integrity verification across a five-word block.
test_cases.Remarks: Platform security interfaces are configured to non-secure prior to enabling interrupts. Transfer completion is detected via an interrupt flag that is cleared in the handler. DMA operations wait until the channel enable register deasserts.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: Initialize the interrupt pending flag to indicate no completion.
Configure the system interface to non-secure by writing 0x1 to the sequence of system registers at fixed addresses in the A1700000 range.
Enable two interrupt sources using the interrupt controller.
Enable both controller-related interrupt sources in the system register block.
Initialize both controller instances by flushing FIFOs, clearing any pending interrupts, and setting device control values.
Program addressing: load the slave address in the target instance and the target address in the master instance; set the byte count to five on both instances.

Set clock parameters for standard timing and additional high-speed timing values on the master instance; program the master code; adjust the interrupt mask to keep transfer complete indications unmasked.
Set transmit and receive FIFO thresholds on both instances.
Enable DMA on the transmitting controller instance.

Prepare the source data buffer in SRAM with a five-word pattern and configure DMA channel 0 for memory-to-peripheral transfer targeting the controller’s block data window; enable the channel and wait until the channel enable register becomes zero.
Start the controller transfer by writing to the transfer control register on the master instance.
Poll the current byte count on the master instance until it reaches zero, inserting short waits between polls.
Wait for the transfer-complete interrupt by repeatedly checking the completion flag and inserting short waits.

In the interrupt handler: acknowledge completion by clearing the controller’s transfer-complete status, clear the platform interrupt controller, clear the corresponding raw system interrupt, insert a short delay, and confirm both the controller status and the raw system status are cleared; on any mismatch increment the test error counter.

Enable DMA reception on the receiving controller instance, then configure DMA channel 1 for peripheral-to-memory transfer from the slave’s block data window into a second SRAM buffer; enable the channel and wait until the channel enable register becomes zero.
Verify data integrity by comparing each of the five words between the source and destination SRAM buffers; accumulate errors on any mismatch.
Insert a short delay and report the final result based on the accumulated errors.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Interrupt handling: a pass requires that a transfer-complete condition is detected; the controller’s interrupt status equals the expected completion value at entry to the handler; after clearing, both the controller status and the corresponding raw system status must be zero.
DMA completion: both transmit and receive DMA operations must deassert the channel enable register, indicating completion.
Data integrity: all five words in the destination SRAM buffer must equal the corresponding words in the source SRAM buffer.
Overall pass requires zero accumulated errors at test end.
test_cases.Hidden_Test_Description: End-to-end I2C0(master) -> I2C1(slave) transfer with DMA on both ends, using interrupts for transfer-complete signaling. Preload 5 words to SRAM_ADDR_1, DMA to MIZAR_I2C0_SMB_HST_BLOCK_DATA, start transfer via MIZAR_I2C0_TSFR_CTRL, wait for Default_IRQHandler to clear MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS and MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0, then DMA from MIZAR_I2C1_SMB_HST_BLOCK_DATA to SRAM_ADDR_2 and compare data.
test_cases.Hidden_Remarks: Before I2C configuration, security NIC registers at 0xA1700008..0xA1700054 are programmed to 0x1 to make LSS NIC non-secure. GIC IRQs 80 and 81 are enabled. LSS system interrupt enable register includes I2C0 and I2C1 interrupt bits. DMA completion is determined by polling MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN until zero. Transfer-complete interrupt is unmasked via MIZAR_I2C0_MASK_INTR (mask value 0xFFFFFFEF).
Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure: FIFO thresholds: write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_TX_FIFO_THLD,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_I2C1_TX_FIFO_THLD,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_RX_FIFO_THLD,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_I2C1_RX_FIFO_THLD,0x5);
Enable DMA on TX side: write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_DMA_CTRL,0x2);
Prepare source buffer: for i=0..4: write_reg(SRAM_ADDR_1 + i*4, i*5) where SRAM_ADDR_1=0xA0243F00.

Configure DMA CH0: write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_CTRL,0x8028028); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_ADDR,0xA0243F00); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_DEST_ADDR,MIZAR_I2C0_SMB_HST_BLOCK_DATA); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_XCNT,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_XMDFY,0x4); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_DEST_XMDFY,0x0); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_REQ,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN,0x1);
Poll: do { data_rd = read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_I2C_CURRENT_BYTECNT); wait_on(100); } while (data_rd != 0);

Default_IRQHandler(): int_pend=0; int_status = read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS); if (int_status == 0x0010) { write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_CLR,0x10); GIC_ClearIRQ(80); GIC_ClearIRQ(81); write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0_I2C0_INTERRUPT); wait_on(100); int_status = read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS); int_status_lss = read_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0) & LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN0_I2C0_INTERRUPT; if (int_status != 0x0 || int_status_lss != 0x0) test_err++; } else { test_err++; }

Configure DMA CH1: write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_CTRL,0x8024028); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_ADDR,MIZAR_I2C1_SMB_HST_BLOCK_DATA); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_DEST_ADDR,0xA0243E00); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_XCNT,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_XMDFY,0x0); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_DEST_XMDFY,0x4); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_REQ,0x6); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN,0x2);
Compare data: for i=0..4: if (read_reg(0xA0243F00 + i*4) != read_reg(0xA0243E00 + i*4)) test_err++;
test_cases.Hidden_Validation_Acceptance_Criteria: Pass if: (1) Default_IRQHandler observes MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS == 0x0010, clears it with MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_CLR=0x10, writes MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0 with LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0_I2C0_INTERRUPT, and after wait both read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS)==0 and (read_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0) & LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN0_I2C0_INTERRUPT)==0; (2) Both DMA phases complete (MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN returns 0 by polling); (3) For i=0..4, read_reg(SRAM_ADDR_1 + 4*i) == read_reg(SRAM_ADDR_2 + 4*i). Any violation increments test_err and leads to nonzero finish(test_err).

test_cases.Test Description: Validate a standard-mode transfer from controller instance 0 (master) to controller instance 1 (slave) using DMA-driven transmit and receive, with interrupt-based completion and post-transfer integrity check over a five-word payload.
test_cases.Remarks: Platform security interfaces are set to non-secure before enabling interrupts. Completion is signaled via an interrupt flag cleared in the handler. DMA operations wait for the channel enable to deassert before proceeding.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: Begin test and prepare local variables.
Configure the system interface to non-secure by writing 0x1 to the series of system registers at fixed addresses in the A1700000 block.
Enable two interrupt sources in the interrupt controller.
Enable both controller-related interrupt sources in the system register block.
Initialize both controller instances by flushing FIFOs, clearing pending interrupts, and setting device control values for standard operation.
Set addressing and transfer length: program the slave address and the master’s target address; set the byte count to five on both instances.
Set standard-mode clock timing parameters on the master instance.
Adjust the interrupt mask to allow transfer-complete signalling.
Set FIFO thresholds on both instances.
Enable DMA on the transmitting controller instance.

Preload a five-word pattern into the source SRAM buffer and configure DMA channel 0 for memory-to-peripheral transfer targeting the master controller’s block data window; enable the channel and wait until the channel enable register indicates completion.
Start the controller transfer by writing to the master’s transfer control register.
Poll the current byte count on the master instance until it reaches zero, inserting longer waits between polls.
Set the interrupt pending flag and wait in a loop until the interrupt handler clears it, inserting short waits.

In the interrupt handler: confirm the transfer-complete status, clear the controller interrupt, clear the platform interrupt controller, clear the raw system interrupt, wait briefly, and confirm that both the controller and system raw status are cleared; on any discrepancy, increment the test error counter.

Enable DMA reception on the receiving controller instance, then configure DMA channel 1 for peripheral-to-memory transfer from the slave controller’s block data window into the destination SRAM buffer; enable the channel and wait until the channel enable register indicates completion.
Verify data integrity by comparing each of the five words between the source and destination SRAM buffers; accumulate errors on any mismatch.
Insert a short delay and report pass or fail based on the accumulated error count.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Interrupt handling: transfer-complete must be observed and cleared; after clearing, both the controller’s interrupt status and the raw system interrupt indication must read as cleared.
DMA completion: both transmit and receive operations must complete as indicated by the channel enable register deasserting.
Data integrity: all five destination words must match the corresponding source words.
Overall pass requires zero accumulated errors.
test_cases.Hidden_Test_Description: Standard-mode I2C0(master) -> I2C1(slave) transfer with DMA TX/RX and interrupt-based completion. Data is preloaded at SRAM_ADDR_1=0xA0243FC0 and transferred to MIZAR_I2C0_SMB_HST_BLOCK_DATA via DMA CH0, I2C transfer is started with MIZAR_I2C0_TSFR_CTRL, IRQ clears MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS and MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0, then DMA CH1 moves MIZAR_I2C1_SMB_HST_BLOCK_DATA to SRAM_ADDR_2=0xA0243FE0, after which data is compared.
test_cases.Hidden_Remarks: Writes 0x1 to 0xA1700008..0xA1700054 to set LSS NIC non-secure. GIC IRQs 80 and 81 are enabled. Interrupts for I2C0 and I2C1 are enabled in MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN0. I2C device control is set to 0x382 for both instances. DMA completion detected by polling MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN until zero. Transfer-complete interrupt allowed via MIZAR_I2C0_MASK_INTR setting 0xFFFFFFEF.
Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure: FIFO thresholds: write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_TX_FIFO_THLD,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_I2C1_TX_FIFO_THLD,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_RX_FIFO_THLD,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_I2C1_RX_FIFO_THLD,0x5);
Enable DMA on TX side: write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_DMA_CTRL,0x2);
Prepare source buffer: for i=0..4: write_reg(0xA0243FC0 + i*4, i*5).

Configure DMA CH0: write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_CTRL,0x8028028); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_ADDR,0xA0243FC0); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_DEST_ADDR,MIZAR_I2C0_SMB_HST_BLOCK_DATA); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_XCNT,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_XMDFY,0x4); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_DEST_XMDFY,0x0); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH0_SRC_REQ,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN,0x1);
Poll: do { data_rd = read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_I2C_CURRENT_BYTECNT); wait_on(5000); } while (data_rd != 0);

Default_IRQHandler(): int_pend=0; int_status = read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS); if (int_status == 0x0010) { write_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_CLR,0x10); GIC_ClearIRQ(80); GIC_ClearIRQ(81); write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0_I2C0_INTERRUPT); wait_on(100); int_status = read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS); int_status_lss = read_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0) & LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN0_I2C0_INTERRUPT; if (int_status != 0x0 || int_status_lss != 0x0) test_err++; } else { test_err++; }

Configure DMA CH1: write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_CTRL,0x8024028); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_ADDR,MIZAR_I2C1_SMB_HST_BLOCK_DATA); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_DEST_ADDR,0xA0243FE0); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_XCNT,0x5); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_XMDFY,0x0); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_DEST_XMDFY,0x4); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_CH1_SRC_REQ,0x6); write_reg(MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN,0x2);
Compare data: for i=0..4: if (read_reg(0xA0243FC0 + i*4) != read_reg(0xA0243FE0 + i*4)) test_err++;
test_cases.Hidden_Validation_Acceptance_Criteria: Pass if: (1) Interrupt path shows MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS == 0x0010, then after clearing with MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_CLR=0x10 and writing MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0, both read_reg(MIZAR_I2C0_INTR_STS)==0 and (read_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR0) & LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN0_I2C0_INTERRUPT)==0; (2) DMA CH0 and CH1 complete (MIZAR_DMA_DMA_CH_EN reads zero by polling); (3) Data at 0xA0243FC0 + 4*i equals data at 0xA0243FE0 + 4*i for i=0..4; else test_err increments and nonzero finish(test_err).
